must_remember: The scalar triple product $a \cdot (b \times c)$ represents the signed volume of the parallelepiped formed by vectors $a$, $b$, and $c$, and is invariant under cyclic permutation.
The vector triple product expands according to the BAC-CAB rule: $a \times (b \times c) = b(a \cdot c) - c(a \cdot b)$.
Vector cross product is non-associative; $a \times (b \times c) \neq (a \times b) \times c$ in general.

The divergence of a curl is identically zero: $\nabla \cdot (\nabla \times A) = 0$ for any continuously twice-differentiable vector field $A$.

glossary.meaning: The dot product of one vector with the cross product of two other vectors, $a \cdot (b \times c)$.
The cross product of a vector with the cross product of two other vectors, $a \times (b \times c)$.
The vector differential operator $\nabla = i(\partial/\partial x) + j(\partial/\partial y) + k(\partial/\partial z)$.
A differential operator measuring the rotational circulation of a vector field, given by $\nabla \times V$.
A differential operator measuring the source or sink strength of a vector field, given by $\nabla \cdot V$.
